stem: What is an Import Set?

options.text: A staging table that holds incoming external data so it can be inspected, transformed, and loaded into a target table.
A live mirror of a production table.
A user's saved query on the incident table.
A type of UI policy.

rationale: Import Sets are staging tables. Incoming data lands there first; transform maps then move and reshape it into the target table. Staging gives you a chance to inspect and transform before touching live data.

distractor_notes.B: Import sets aren't mirrors of production tables.
distractor_notes.C: Saved queries are stored on sys_user_filter or similar — not import sets.
distractor_notes.D: UI policies govern form behavior.

stem: What is a Data Source in the import-set workflow?

options.text: A configuration record that describes where incoming data comes from (file upload, FTP, JDBC, REST, etc.) and how to fetch and parse it.
A row in the audit history.
A category on a KB article.
A favorite saved by the user.

rationale: Data Sources tell the platform where the data is coming from and how to retrieve and parse it — file, FTP, REST, JDBC, etc. They feed import sets, which feed transform maps.

distractor_notes.B: Audit rows are change history.
distractor_notes.C: KB categories are unrelated.
distractor_notes.D: Favorites are nav shortcuts.

stem: An admin needs to load a CSV of vendors into the platform. Which sequence is the textbook approach?

options.text: Create a Data Source pointing at the CSV → Load the data into an Import Set staging table → Build a Transform Map to the target table → Run the transform.
Edit the production table by hand to add the rows one by one.
Open the CSV in a browser tab and copy values into incidents.
Move the CSV to a KB article.

rationale: Data Source → Import Set → Transform Map → Target is the canonical pipeline. Each step is inspectable and reusable.

distractor_notes.B: Manual editing doesn't scale and skips every safeguard.
distractor_notes.C: Copy/paste isn't a supported pattern.
distractor_notes.D: KBs aren't data targets.

stem: Why does the platform use a staging Import Set table instead of writing directly to the target?

options.text: Staging lets you inspect raw data, run validations, apply transformations, handle errors, and re-run without dirtying the target table.
Because the target table cannot accept writes.
Because import sets are encrypted and target tables are not.
Because the target table is read-only.

rationale: Staging is the point: it lets you transform, validate, and recover before the data lands in the target. Without it, errors get expensive fast.

distractor_notes.B: Target tables accept writes; the staging step is an architectural choice.
distractor_notes.C: Encryption isn't the reason.
distractor_notes.D: Target tables aren't read-only.

stem: Which file format is NOT directly supported as an Import Set data source out-of-the-box?

options.text: A live Microsoft Word .docx with table data.
CSV
Excel (XLS/XLSX)
XML / JSON

rationale: Out-of-the-box import data sources support CSV, Excel, XML/JSON, and similar structured formats — plus JDBC, REST, FTP. Word documents are document format, not a structured data source.

distractor_notes.B: CSV is supported.
distractor_notes.C: Excel (XLS/XLSX) is supported.
distractor_notes.D: XML / JSON are supported.

stem: An import has been running for a few days and the import set staging tables have grown large. What's the supported way to keep things tidy?

options.text: Use the platform's import set cleanup mechanism (e.g., scheduled cleanup or table rotation) to prune old staging rows after successful transforms.
Disable the import permanently.
Delete the target table to start over.
Lower the size of every monitor in the office.

rationale: Import set staging rows accumulate. The platform supports cleanup so old runs don't bloat the staging tables indefinitely.

distractor_notes.B: Disabling halts the work but doesn't clean.
distractor_notes.C: Deleting the target nukes the legitimate data.
distractor_notes.D: Monitor size is unrelated.

stem: Which statement is most accurate about applying ACLs to import data?

options.text: ACLs evaluate at insert/update on the target table when transforms write records, the same way they evaluate any other write — so import users still need the right permissions.
Imports bypass all ACLs by design.
ACLs apply only after the import is committed for a week.
ACLs only apply if the import is run by a guest user.

rationale: Transforms write to the target like any other server-side write, and ACLs evaluate accordingly. Import users (or the configured run-as user) need the right permissions on the target — otherwise the writes fail.

distractor_notes.B: Imports don't bypass ACLs.
distractor_notes.C: ACLs evaluate at write-time, not on a delay.
distractor_notes.D: Guest users are a different (typically unauthenticated) context entirely.

stem: A nightly file lands on an SFTP server and must be ingested. Which data source configuration fits best?

options.text: Configure a Data Source of type SFTP (or FTP/FTPS) pointing at the file path, with credentials and a schedule to retrieve and parse it.
Manually download the file and copy/paste into a KB article.
Skip the data source and write a CSS rule to display the file.
Email the file to every user.

rationale: The platform supports FTP-family protocols as data sources, with schedules and credentials. That's the right shape for a nightly drop on SFTP.

distractor_notes.B: Manual handling doesn't scale.
distractor_notes.C: CSS doesn't parse data files.
distractor_notes.D: Emailing files to everyone is a security and noise problem.

stem: A transform run reports 200 errors and 800 successful inserts. What's the right next step?

options.text: Inspect the import set rows with errors, fix the data or refine the transform map, and re-run the failed rows without re-importing the entire data set.
Delete the target table and start over.
Ignore the errors and disable error logging.
Run the import 10 more times and hope it works.

rationale: Staging exists exactly for this. Inspect the failing rows, fix the input or the transform, and re-process only the errors. No need to re-import everything.

distractor_notes.B: Deleting the target nukes successful imports too.
distractor_notes.C: Hiding errors doesn't fix them.
distractor_notes.D: Re-running without understanding doesn't fix anything.

stem: Which statement about Import Set rows is most accurate?

options.text: Each staging row corresponds to a record from the source data and has a state showing whether the transform inserted, updated, ignored, or errored on it.
Staging rows are written directly to the target table.
Staging rows live forever and cannot be deleted.
Staging rows are visible only to the system admin user.

rationale: Each staging row tracks what happened to it during the transform — useful for both auditing and re-running just the failed rows.

distractor_notes.B: Staging is separate from the target.
distractor_notes.C: Staging rows can be cleaned up.
distractor_notes.D: Visibility depends on role/ACL, not just admin.

stem: An admin wants the first row of an uploaded CSV to be treated as column headers. Where is this configured?

options.text: On the Data Source's parsing configuration (e.g., headers in first row option) so the platform maps columns by header name.
On the user's profile.
On the favicon.svg.
On the incident table form layout.

rationale: Parsing options on the Data Source — including whether the first row is headers, what delimiter to use, and what character encoding to assume — control how the file is interpreted.

distractor_notes.B: User profile doesn't influence CSV parsing.
distractor_notes.C: Favicon is unrelated.
distractor_notes.D: Form layout doesn't change imports.

stem: A team is migrating user records from a legacy system. They plan to run weekly delta loads after the initial full load. Which approach is most appropriate?

options.text: Reuse the Data Source and Transform Map for both initial and weekly delta loads, using coalesce fields on the transform map to update existing users and insert new ones.
Build two completely different pipelines so nothing is shared.
Always run a full reload from scratch every week.
Disable the user table during deltas.

rationale: Coalesce on the transform map makes the same pipeline handle both initial and delta loads — match by a stable key, update existing, insert new. Reusing the artifacts keeps maintenance manageable.

distractor_notes.B: Duplicate pipelines drift.
distractor_notes.C: Weekly full reloads waste resources and can churn user records.
distractor_notes.D: Disabling the table breaks dependent workflows.

stem: What is a Transform Map?

options.text: A configuration that maps fields from an Import Set's staging table to fields on a target table, with rules for coalescing, scripts, and field-level transformations.
A type of business rule that fires on form load.
A KB article that explains how to import data.
A scheduled job that emails the data dictionary.

rationale: Transform Maps define how each source column maps to each target field, plus how to identify existing records via coalesce, plus optional scripts at the row/field/event level.

distractor_notes.B: Business rules and transform maps are different mechanisms.
distractor_notes.C: A KB article documents; it doesn't transform.
distractor_notes.D: Scheduled jobs aren't transform maps.

stem: What is a Field Map within a Transform Map?

options.text: A row that says 'source column X' maps to 'target field Y', optionally with a script for value transformation.
A type of UI policy.
A pointer between two unrelated tables.
A free-text field on the user record.

rationale: Field Maps are the individual pairings inside a Transform Map. Each one says how one source column lands on one target field, with optional scripting in between.

distractor_notes.B: UI policy is form behavior.
distractor_notes.C: Field maps are inside a transform map, not random table pointers.
distractor_notes.D: Free-text fields aren't field maps.

stem: What does the Coalesce attribute on a Field Map do?

options.text: Marks the field as a match key — if a target record exists with the same value, the transform updates it; otherwise it inserts a new record.
Encrypts the value in transit.
Forces the value to uppercase.
Removes the field from the import.

rationale: Coalesce defines the match key for the transform. If the target table has a row matching the coalesce value, the transform updates that row. If not, it inserts a new one. This is how the same pipeline supports both updates and inserts.

distractor_notes.B: Coalesce is a match rule, not encryption.
distractor_notes.C: Case folding is a separate transformation step.
distractor_notes.D: Coalesce includes the field; it doesn't remove it.

stem: An admin wants user records imported with the same employee_number to update existing rows rather than create duplicates. What configuration achieves this?

options.text: Mark the field map for employee_number as a Coalesce field on the transform map.
Set the target table to read-only.
Delete the user table before each import.
Disable ACLs during import.

rationale: Coalesce on employee_number says 'if a row with this number exists, update; else insert.' Exactly the upsert behavior the admin wants.

distractor_notes.B: Read-only would block the upsert.
distractor_notes.C: Deleting before import loses every other field's history.
distractor_notes.D: Disabling ACLs is a security disaster and doesn't help.

stem: What happens when a Transform Map has multiple Coalesce fields?

options.text: All coalesce fields together form a composite match key — the transform matches a target only when all coalesce values match.
Only the first coalesce is used and the rest are ignored.
Each coalesce field creates a separate duplicate record.
Multiple coalesce fields are not supported.

rationale: Multiple coalesce fields form a composite key. A target row matches only when every coalesce field matches. Useful when no single column is unique on its own.

distractor_notes.B: All coalesce fields contribute to the match.
distractor_notes.C: Coalesce prevents duplicates, not creates them.
distractor_notes.D: Composite coalesce is supported and common.

stem: Which Transform Map script type runs once before any row is processed?

options.text: onStart
onBefore
onAfter
onComplete

rationale: onStart fires once at the beginning of the transform run — useful for setting up counters, looking up reference data, or one-time logging.

distractor_notes.B: onBefore runs before each row.
distractor_notes.C: onAfter runs after each row.
distractor_notes.D: onComplete runs once after all rows.

stem: Which Transform Map script type runs per-row before the row is inserted/updated on the target?

options.text: onBefore
onStart
onComplete
onSubmit

rationale: onBefore runs for each row before the target write. It's where you'd transform values, set defaults, look up references, or decide to skip the row entirely.

distractor_notes.B: onStart runs once before any rows.
distractor_notes.C: onComplete runs once after all rows.
distractor_notes.D: onSubmit is a UI/Client Script concept, not a transform script type.

stem: A transform map needs to skip rows whose Status column is 'archived' so they aren't loaded into the target. Which script type and pattern is the right fit?

options.text: An onBefore script that inspects source.u_status and sets ignore = true (or similar) so the row is skipped during the transform.
A UI policy that hides the row on the form.
Deleting every archived row from the production table after the import.
Renaming the column to 'maybe_skip'.

rationale: onBefore is where per-row filtering belongs. Inspect the source, decide whether to process, and skip when the rule says skip — all before the target write.

distractor_notes.B: Form UI policies don't affect imports.
distractor_notes.C: Cleanup after the fact is brittle and expensive.
distractor_notes.D: Renaming columns doesn't filter.

stem: A source column contains a free-text department name ('Engineering', 'engineering', 'ENG'). The target field is a reference to the Department table. How is this typically handled in a Field Map?

options.text: Use a script on the Field Map (or an onBefore script) to look up the Department by normalized name and set the target reference to the sys_id of the matching record.
Paste the literal string into the reference field.
Set the target field to type Boolean.
Skip the column and forget about departments.

rationale: Reference fields need sys_ids, not strings. A script normalizes the source string, looks up the matching record, and sets the reference. That bridges loose string input to clean relational data.

distractor_notes.B: Reference fields don't take literal strings.
distractor_notes.C: Boolean can't represent a department.
distractor_notes.D: Skipping the data abandons the requirement.

stem: A transform inserts the same record twice on each run because the file repeats the row. What's the most appropriate fix?

options.text: Configure a Coalesce field on the natural key (e.g., employee_number) so the second occurrence updates the existing record instead of inserting a duplicate.
Disable inserts entirely on the target table.
Set the target field to read-only.
Delete duplicates after the run with a script.

rationale: Duplicates are a missing match-key. Coalesce on the natural key tells the transform to treat repeats as updates. Cleaner than after-the-fact deletes.

distractor_notes.B: Disabling inserts breaks the legitimate flow.
distractor_notes.C: Read-only blocks the update path too.
distractor_notes.D: Post-run cleanup is fragile and slow.

stem: Which statement about scheduled transforms is most accurate?

options.text: Data sources and transform maps can be scheduled together so a recurring import + transform runs without manual intervention.
Transforms must always be triggered manually.
Transforms only run when the admin is logged in.
Transforms cannot be scheduled at all.

rationale: Scheduled imports + transforms are a built-in pattern. The platform pulls/parses the source on a schedule and runs the transform automatically.

distractor_notes.B: Scheduling is supported.
distractor_notes.C: Server-side jobs don't require interactive presence.
distractor_notes.D: Scheduling is well-supported.

stem: A transform that runs scripts per row is slow on large imports. What's a sensible first step?

options.text: Move work that doesn't need per-row context (lookups, configuration loads) into onStart and onComplete; inside per-row scripts, cache lookups and avoid heavy queries.
Delete every row that failed once.
Disable the target table during imports.
Always re-import every record from scratch.

rationale: Per-row scripts amplify costs. Push lookups and setup into onStart/onComplete, cache where possible, and keep the per-row work tight. That's the classic transform performance pattern.

distractor_notes.B: Deleting failed rows isn't a perf fix.
distractor_notes.C: Disabling the target breaks the import.
distractor_notes.D: Full reloads make things worse.

stem: What does ServiceNow's Inbound REST API provide?

options.text: HTTP endpoints (e.g., /api/now/table/incident) that external systems use to create, read, update, and delete records on the instance with JSON payloads.
A way to log in to the instance using a USB key.
A read-only feed of the platform's marketing pages.
A scheduled job that emails records.

rationale: Inbound REST exposes the instance's tables (and custom endpoints) over HTTP with JSON. External systems use it to push and pull data — the canonical 'how things talk to ServiceNow' interface.

distractor_notes.B: USB key login isn't a thing here.
distractor_notes.C: Marketing pages aren't the REST API.
distractor_notes.D: Scheduled jobs aren't REST endpoints.

stem: What is the Outbound REST Web Service used for?

options.text: Letting the instance call external HTTP/JSON APIs — for integrations, notifications, lookups, and triggering external systems.
Sending physical mail.
Sending push notifications to mobile devices only.
Replacing the user's browser.

rationale: Outbound REST is the platform's mechanism for calling external HTTP APIs. Use it from Flow Designer, scripts, or business rules to push data or fetch from another system.

distractor_notes.B: Physical mail is unrelated.
distractor_notes.C: Push notifications are a separate channel.
distractor_notes.D: The browser isn't replaced.

stem: Which statement is most accurate about SOAP web services on the platform?

options.text: SOAP is supported (both inbound and outbound) for compatibility with systems that require it, although REST is generally preferred for new integrations.
SOAP is not supported in any direction.
SOAP is the only supported integration protocol.
SOAP only works inside the user's browser.

rationale: SOAP support is still there — important for legacy integrations. New work typically uses REST because it's lighter and easier to debug, but SOAP isn't going anywhere yet.

distractor_notes.B: SOAP is supported.
distractor_notes.C: REST exists alongside SOAP.
distractor_notes.D: SOAP runs server-to-server.

stem: What is a MID Server?

options.text: A Java application installed on a customer's network that acts as a bridge between the ServiceNow instance and on-premises systems behind the corporate firewall.
A browser plugin installed on every user's laptop.
A type of ACL.
A scheduled job that emails the admin.

rationale: MID Server is the bridge into the customer's internal network. The instance (cloud) talks to MID; MID reaches into on-prem systems on its behalf. It's how Discovery, IntegrationHub, and JDBC imports reach private systems.

distractor_notes.B: Browser plugins are unrelated.
distractor_notes.C: MID Servers aren't ACLs.
distractor_notes.D: Scheduled jobs run inside the instance, not on a MID Server.

stem: A team wants to pull data from an on-prem SQL database into ServiceNow without exposing the DB to the public internet. What's the typical pattern?

options.text: Install a MID Server inside the corporate network, configure a JDBC data source through the MID Server, and have the instance read via MID.
Move the database to the public internet.
Have the admin email the SQL results daily.
Copy/paste rows from a SQL client into a KB article.

rationale: MID Server is the supported pattern for reaching private databases. The DB stays inside the network; the MID Server queries it and relays the data to the instance.

distractor_notes.B: Internet-exposing a corporate DB is unsafe.
distractor_notes.C: Manual emailing doesn't scale or audit well.
distractor_notes.D: Copy/paste isn't an integration pattern.

stem: What is IntegrationHub?

options.text: A framework that extends Flow Designer with integration capabilities — including spokes (pre-built integration packs), custom actions, and connection management — for connecting to external systems with low code.
A type of incident.
A read-only audit log of plugin activations.
A scheduled job for sending email.

rationale: IntegrationHub is the platform's integration story for Flow Designer. Spokes pre-build the actions for popular external systems; custom actions cover the rest; connections manage credentials and endpoints. Low-code integration as a first-class pattern.

distractor_notes.B: Not an incident.
distractor_notes.C: Not an audit log.
distractor_notes.D: Not a scheduled job.

stem: What is a spoke in IntegrationHub?

options.text: A scoped application that packages pre-built actions and integration capabilities for a specific external system (e.g., a Slack spoke, a Microsoft Teams spoke).
A wheel on a server rack.
A new field type.
A type of UI policy.

rationale: A spoke bundles ready-made actions targeting a specific system — install, configure the connection, and you've got low-code actions to use inside flows.

distractor_notes.B: Different kind of spoke.
distractor_notes.C: Not a field type.
distractor_notes.D: Not a UI policy.

stem: An external system needs to retrieve a single incident by sys_id over REST. Which endpoint shape is correct?

options.text: GET /api/now/table/incident/{sys_id}
DELETE /api/now/table/incident/{sys_id}
POST /api/now/table/incident
PUT /api/now/table/incident

rationale: Table API uses GET on /api/now/table/incident/{sys_id} for retrieve-by-id. POST creates, PATCH/PUT updates, DELETE deletes — REST verb semantics map to the underlying operations.

distractor_notes.B: DELETE would remove the record.
distractor_notes.C: POST creates a new record.
distractor_notes.D: PUT updates a record (typically with full body).

stem: A partner system will call ServiceNow REST APIs on behalf of itself, not a specific user. What authentication is appropriate?

options.text: OAuth (client credentials) with a dedicated service-account scope and least-privilege roles, rotating secrets per policy.
Use the admin's personal password embedded in the partner's code.
Disable authentication on REST endpoints.
Send the password as a URL query parameter.

rationale: Machine-to-machine integrations belong on OAuth client credentials with a dedicated service account, least-privilege roles, and secret rotation. That's how you make integrations safe and auditable.

distractor_notes.B: Embedding personal passwords is unsafe and unauditable.
distractor_notes.C: Open APIs are an instant breach.
distractor_notes.D: Passwords in URLs leak through logs and history.

stem: A team needs to call a partner's REST API from a flow. They want low-code if possible and don't mind installing a spoke if it exists. What's the right first move?

options.text: Check whether an IntegrationHub spoke exists for that partner; if so, install and configure it, and use its actions inside the flow. Otherwise build a custom action wrapping a REST step.
Write the entire flow as a single business rule with raw fetch calls.
Run a scheduled job that uses curl on a MID Server.
Ignore the requirement.

rationale: Spokes are the low-code path. If one exists, use it; if not, a custom action wrapping the REST step keeps the integration inside Flow Designer's framework rather than spilling into ad-hoc scripts.

distractor_notes.B: Raw business rules dodge the integration framework.
distractor_notes.C: curl on a MID Server is wildly off the supported path.
distractor_notes.D: Ignoring isn't an option.

stem: Which response format does the Table API return by default for GET requests?

options.text: JSON
Plain text
PDF
CSV (always)

rationale: Table API responses are JSON by default. XML is supported via Accept headers; CSV/Excel are supported in other contexts. JSON is the default and the most common.

distractor_notes.B: Plain text isn't the default.
distractor_notes.C: PDF isn't a Table API response.
distractor_notes.D: CSV isn't the default.

stem: A team is installing a new MID Server in production. What's the most appropriate posture for the MID Server's user/account?

options.text: Use a dedicated MID Server user account with the minimum roles required, rotate credentials per policy, and monitor MID Server activity.
Use a personal admin account and share the credentials with the whole team.
Disable authentication on the MID Server.
Run the MID Server as root with no auditing.

rationale: Dedicated service account with least privilege is the standard, supportable posture. Personal accounts conflate ownership with operation; disabled auth is a non-starter.

distractor_notes.B: Personal accounts make audits painful and access fragile to staffing changes.
distractor_notes.C: Disabled auth is wide-open.
distractor_notes.D: Root with no auditing is an audit failure waiting to happen.

stem: Which Import Set data source type retrieves a file from an FTP or SFTP server on a schedule?

options.text: HTTP
File (FTP/SFTP)
JDBC
Email

rationale: The File (FTP/SFTP) data source type is configured to retrieve a file from an FTP or SFTP server, enabling scheduled automated ingestion of files placed on remote servers.

distractor_notes.A: HTTP data sources retrieve content from a web URL, not FTP/SFTP.
distractor_notes.C: JDBC data sources connect directly to a relational database, not a file server.
distractor_notes.D: Email data sources process inbound email content, not FTP/SFTP files.

stem: What is the purpose of the Import Set staging table?

options.text: To permanently store all imported records as a data archive
To hold raw imported data temporarily before it is transformed into the target table
To validate imported data against ACL rules
To replicate data to a secondary instance

rationale: The Import Set staging table temporarily holds raw imported data. The transform map then processes these rows and writes them to the target table. The staging table acts as a buffer between the source data and the target.

distractor_notes.A: Import Set tables are temporary staging areas, not permanent archives.
distractor_notes.C: ACL validation happens on target table records, not the staging table.
distractor_notes.D: Import Sets are for data ingestion, not instance replication.

stem: What are the possible row states for an Import Set row after a transform run?

options.text: Success, Failed, Skipped, Ignored
Inserted, Updated, Deleted, Errored
Inserted, Updated, Ignored, Error
Committed, Rolled Back, Pending

rationale: After a transform, each Import Set row receives a state of Inserted (new record created), Updated (existing record modified), Ignored (row skipped per script logic), or Error (transform failed for that row).

distractor_notes.A: 'Skipped' and 'Failed' are not the standard row state labels.
distractor_notes.B: 'Deleted' and 'Errored' are not the standard row states for Import Sets.
distractor_notes.D: Committed/Rolled Back are database transaction concepts, not Import Set row states.

stem: What is a JDBC data source in the context of ServiceNow Import Sets?

options.text: A connection to a remote REST API endpoint
A direct database connection that queries a relational database to retrieve records for import
A file-based source that reads CSV files from a local directory
A connection to a SOAP web service

rationale: A JDBC (Java Database Connectivity) data source establishes a direct connection to a relational database system (such as Oracle, SQL Server, or MySQL) to retrieve records for import into ServiceNow via Import Sets.

distractor_notes.A: REST API connections use the REST data source type, not JDBC.
distractor_notes.C: CSV files use the File or HTTP data source types.
distractor_notes.D: SOAP connections use the SOAP web service data source type.

stem: An import run completes with 500 Ignored rows. What is the most likely cause?

options.text: The coalesce field found matching records and skipped the update because nothing changed
A transform script returned IGNORE for those rows based on a condition
The data source file was corrupted for those rows
The user running the import lacked write access to the target table

rationale: Ignored rows in an Import Set transform run are typically caused by a transform script (onBefore, onTransform) explicitly returning IGNORE, instructing the system to skip processing of that row.

distractor_notes.A: Coalesce matching that finds no changes typically results in an Updated row with no changes, not Ignored.
distractor_notes.C: Corrupted rows would typically result in Error state, not Ignored.
distractor_notes.D: ACL issues would cause errors, not Ignored rows.

stem: Which Transform Map script type runs once after ALL rows have been processed?

options.text: onBefore
onStart
onAfter
onComplete

rationale: The onComplete script in a Transform Map runs once after all rows have been processed, making it suitable for post-import cleanup, summary logging, or sending a completion notification.

distractor_notes.A: onBefore runs per row, before the row is transformed.
distractor_notes.B: onStart runs once before any rows are processed (pre-transform initialization).
distractor_notes.C: onAfter runs per row, after the row has been transformed.

stem: What does a Reference Lookup in a Transform Map Field Map do?

options.text: It validates the field value against a list of allowed values
It looks up a record in another table by a specified field to resolve a reference field value
It creates a new record in the target table if no match is found
It copies the field value verbatim without transformation

rationale: A Reference Lookup in a Field Map resolves a reference field by looking up a record in the referenced table using a specified field value (e.g., finding a User record by email address to populate the Assigned To field).

distractor_notes.A: Choice field validation is a different mechanism; Reference Lookup resolves reference fields.
distractor_notes.C: Creating a new record on no match is an option on the transform map, not specifically a Reference Lookup behavior.
distractor_notes.D: Copying verbatim is a direct field map without any lookup.

stem: Which Table API endpoint retrieves a list of records from a specified table?

options.text: GET /api/now/table/{tableName}/{sys_id}
GET /api/now/table/{tableName}
POST /api/now/table/{tableName}
GET /api/now/attachment/{tableName}

rationale: The GET /api/now/table/{tableName} endpoint retrieves multiple records from the specified table. Adding /{sys_id} at the end retrieves a single specific record.

distractor_notes.A: Including /{sys_id} retrieves a single record, not a list.
distractor_notes.C: POST creates a new record, it does not retrieve records.
distractor_notes.D: The attachment endpoint is for file attachments, not table records.

stem: Which Table API parameter limits the number of records returned in a GET request?

options.text: sysparm_fields
sysparm_query
sysparm_limit
sysparm_count

rationale: The sysparm_limit parameter in a Table API GET request controls the maximum number of records returned. For example, sysparm_limit=10 returns at most 10 records.

distractor_notes.A: sysparm_fields controls which fields are returned in the response, not the record count.
distractor_notes.B: sysparm_query filters records by condition, not by count.
distractor_notes.D: sysparm_count is used to return only the count of matching records, not to limit a list result.

stem: After a transform run, what does the Import Set log show?

options.text: A record for each user who accessed the import set
Details of each row's transform result including state, errors, and target record sys_id
The business rules that fired during the transform
A diff of changes made to system properties during the import

rationale: The Import Set log provides details of each row's transform outcome, including its final state (Inserted, Updated, Ignored, Error), any error messages, and a link to the created or updated target record.

distractor_notes.A: User access logs are captured in the system audit, not the Import Set log.
distractor_notes.C: Business rule execution details are in the system log, not the Import Set transform log.
distractor_notes.D: System property changes are tracked in the update set, not the Import Set log.

stem: Which Table API parameter excludes reference link information from the response to reduce payload size?

options.text: sysparm_no_links=true
sysparm_excludeReferenceLink=true
sysparm_fields=no_ref
sysparm_references=false

rationale: sysparm_excludeReferenceLink=true removes the link property from reference fields in the response, reducing payload size when the caller only needs the display value or sys_id.

distractor_notes.A: sysparm_no_links is not a documented Table API parameter.
distractor_notes.C: sysparm_fields=no_ref is not a valid parameter value.
distractor_notes.D: sysparm_references=false is not the documented parameter; sysparm_excludeReferenceLink is.

stem: What is a MID Server cluster used for?

options.text: Running multiple ServiceNow instances on the same hardware
Providing high availability and load distribution across multiple MID Servers for a single function
Grouping unrelated MID Servers for management purposes only
Isolating MID Servers into separate network zones

rationale: A MID Server cluster groups multiple MID Servers to provide high availability and load distribution. If one MID Server in a cluster becomes unavailable, others in the cluster continue processing work.

distractor_notes.A: MID Servers are agents on customer networks, not ServiceNow instance hosts.
distractor_notes.C: Clustering provides active redundancy, not just management grouping.
distractor_notes.D: Network zone isolation is an infrastructure concept separate from MID Server clustering.

stem: What is the purpose of the 'Target table' field on a Transform Map?

options.text: Specifies the Import Set staging table to read from
Specifies the ServiceNow table where transformed records will be created or updated
Defines which fields are mandatory in the imported data
Sets the role required to run the transform

rationale: The Target table field on a Transform Map defines which ServiceNow table (e.g., sys_user, incident) will receive the records after transformation. The transform map maps source columns to target table fields.

distractor_notes.A: The Import Set staging table is the source; Target table is the destination.
distractor_notes.C: Mandatory field definitions are in the data dictionary, not the transform map target table setting.
distractor_notes.D: Role requirements for running transforms are not defined on the transform map's target table field.

stem: A developer wants to retrieve the display value of the 'assigned_to' reference field (the user's name) rather than their sys_id from the Table API. Which parameter achieves this?

options.text: sysparm_fields=assigned_to.name
sysparm_display_value=true
sysparm_resolve_refs=true
sysparm_reference_format=display

rationale: Setting sysparm_display_value=true causes the Table API to return display values (like a user's full name) for reference and choice fields instead of their internal values (sys_ids or raw choice values).

distractor_notes.A: sysparm_fields controls which fields are returned, not the value format of reference fields.
distractor_notes.C: sysparm_resolve_refs is not a documented Table API parameter.
distractor_notes.D: sysparm_reference_format is not a documented Table API parameter.

stem: How does a scheduled import using a data source and transform map typically execute in ServiceNow?

options.text: A Scheduled Job triggers the load and transform steps automatically
A user must manually click Load and Transform each time
The MID Server initiates the import on its own schedule
An email notification triggers the import when the source file arrives

rationale: Scheduled imports use a Scheduled Job that automatically triggers the data source load and transform map execution at the configured interval, enabling hands-free recurring data ingestion.

distractor_notes.B: Manual triggering defeats the purpose of scheduling; scheduled imports run automatically.
distractor_notes.C: MID Servers facilitate connectivity but do not independently schedule import runs.
distractor_notes.D: Email-triggered imports would require a custom integration; scheduled imports use Scheduled Jobs.

stem: What is the Aggregate API in ServiceNow used for?

options.text: Combining multiple REST requests into a single batch request
Performing aggregate operations like COUNT, SUM, AVG on table data
Aggregating records from multiple tables into a single response
Compressing REST API responses to reduce bandwidth

rationale: The ServiceNow Aggregate API (/api/now/stats/{tableName}) allows callers to perform aggregate operations such as COUNT, SUM, MIN, MAX, and AVG on table data, useful for reporting and statistics without retrieving individual records.

distractor_notes.A: Batch requests are handled by the Batch API, not the Aggregate API.
distractor_notes.C: Aggregating across multiple tables is not the function of the Aggregate API.
distractor_notes.D: Response compression is an HTTP-level concern, not an API feature.

stem: An admin sets up a nightly CSV import of cost center data into a custom table. The next morning, 300 rows show as Updated but the manager field is blank for all of them. What is the most likely cause?

options.text: The coalesce field matched records and the manager field was not in the source CSV
A UI Policy is hiding the manager field in the form view
The target table's manager field is read-only via an ACL
The MID Server was offline during the import

rationale: If the source CSV does not include the manager column, or the transform map does not have a field map for the manager field, the existing manager value would be left unchanged (or blanked if overwrite is configured). The most likely cause here is the manager field not being in the source data or mapped.

distractor_notes.B: UI Policies affect form display, not data import outcomes.
distractor_notes.C: If the ACL blocked the write, the rows would show as Error, not Updated.
distractor_notes.D: A MID Server outage would prevent the import from running at all; 300 Updated rows means the import ran successfully.

stem: A source CSV contains department names like 'engineering', 'Engineering', and 'ENGINEERING' that must all map to the same Choice value 'Engineering' in the target table. Which transform map feature handles this normalization?

options.text: A coalesce field set on the department column ensures case-insensitive matching against the target table
A choice action of 'Translate' combined with a transform script that calls .toLowerCase() and then capitalizes the first letter
A Reference Lookup against the sys_choice table to find the canonical label value
A Field Map script on the department field that normalizes the value to the correct case before the choice action evaluates it

rationale: A Field Map script can transform the raw source value before it is evaluated by the choice action. Running a normalization script (e.g., lowercase then capitalize) ensures that all variants map to the correct canonical choice value.

distractor_notes.A: Coalesce is for deduplication against the target table based on a matching field, not for normalizing text case within a field value.
distractor_notes.B: A 'Translate' choice action and a separate script are not a built-in combination; the transform script on the field map is the right mechanism.
distractor_notes.C: sys_choice lookup would only confirm the choice exists, not normalize inconsistent incoming values.

stem: What does the 'Content-Type: application/json' header tell the ServiceNow Table API when included in a POST request?

options.text: That the caller wants the response returned in JSON format
That the request body is formatted as JSON, so the API should parse it as JSON
That the API should compress the response using JSON encoding
That the caller is using OAuth token authentication

rationale: The Content-Type header tells the server how the request body is formatted. Setting it to application/json instructs the Table API to parse the incoming request body as JSON.

distractor_notes.A: The response format preference is communicated through the Accept header, not Content-Type.
distractor_notes.C: Content-Type describes the body format, not compression — compression uses the Accept-Encoding header.
distractor_notes.D: Authentication is communicated through the Authorization header, not Content-Type.

stem: Which operating systems does ServiceNow support for MID Server installation?

options.text: Windows only
Linux only
Windows and Linux (both supported)
macOS, Windows, and Linux

rationale: ServiceNow MID Server supports installation on both Windows and Linux operating systems, giving organizations flexibility to deploy on their existing server infrastructure.

distractor_notes.A: Limiting to Windows is incorrect; Linux is also fully supported and commonly used.
distractor_notes.B: Linux-only is incorrect; Windows is also a fully supported MID Server platform.
distractor_notes.D: macOS is not a supported MID Server OS; only Windows and Linux are officially supported.

stem: What is the recommended approach for cleaning up large Import Set staging tables that have accumulated rows over many import runs?

options.text: Manually delete rows using a GlideRecord script in a background script
Use the 'Clean up import sets' scheduled job or the cleanup option on the Import Set record to remove processed rows
Drop and recreate the staging table after each import run
Export the rows to a CSV and then truncate the table directly in the database

rationale: ServiceNow provides a built-in 'Clean up import sets' mechanism (available as a scheduled job or manual option) to remove processed rows from staging tables, keeping them manageable without direct database manipulation.

distractor_notes.A: While a GlideRecord script could work, it is not the recommended built-in approach for routine cleanup.
distractor_notes.C: Dropping and recreating the table would destroy the table definition and transform map relationships.
distractor_notes.D: Direct database truncation bypasses ServiceNow's application layer and is not a supported maintenance approach.

stem: An external system makes a GET request to /api/now/table/incident and receives 10,000 records. The developer wants to retrieve only records where active=true and only 3 fields (number, short_description, assigned_to). Which parameter combination is correct?

options.text: sysparm_query=active=true&sysparm_fields=number,short_description,assigned_to
sysparm_filter=active:true&sysparm_select=number|short_description|assigned_to
sysparm_query=active==true&sysparm_columns=number;short_description;assigned_to
filter=active=true&fields=number,short_description,assigned_to

rationale: sysparm_query uses encoded query syntax (active=true) and sysparm_fields accepts a comma-separated list of field names. Together they filter records and limit the response payload efficiently.

distractor_notes.B: sysparm_filter and sysparm_select are not valid Table API parameters; the correct names are sysparm_query and sysparm_fields.
distractor_notes.C: sysparm_query uses single = (not ==) for equality, and sysparm_columns is not the correct parameter name for field selection.
distractor_notes.D: filter= and fields= without the sysparm_ prefix are not valid Table API parameter names.

stem: What file describes the operations, input parameters, and output structure of a SOAP web service?

options.text: JSON Schema file
OpenAPI/Swagger specification
WSDL (Web Services Description Language) file
XSD (XML Schema Definition) file

rationale: A WSDL (Web Services Description Language) file describes a SOAP web service's operations, the parameters required for each operation, and the structure of input/output messages, allowing clients to understand and consume the service.

distractor_notes.A: JSON Schema describes JSON data structures, not SOAP services.
distractor_notes.B: OpenAPI/Swagger describes REST APIs, not SOAP services.
distractor_notes.D: XSD describes XML document structure and is often referenced by a WSDL but is not itself the service description.

stem: A developer wants to create a reusable integration action that calls a Slack API to post messages and can be used across multiple flows. What is the correct IntegrationHub construct to build?

options.text: A Subflow that contains a hardcoded Slack API REST call and is shared via a Flow Designer template
A custom IntegrationHub Action with a REST Step configured for the Slack API, published as a reusable spoke action
A Business Rule that triggers on any record update and calls the Slack API using GlideHTTPRequest
A Scheduled Job that periodically checks for new records and posts updates to Slack

rationale: A custom IntegrationHub Action with a REST Step is the correct construct for a reusable, flow-callable integration unit. It encapsulates the Slack API call and its inputs/outputs, making it consumable across multiple flows like a spoke action.

distractor_notes.A: Subflows are for orchestrating multi-step processes, not for encapsulating a single API call as a reusable action primitive.
distractor_notes.C: A Business Rule with GlideHTTPRequest is a valid scripted approach but is less reusable, harder to maintain, and bypasses the low-code IntegrationHub approach.
distractor_notes.D: A Scheduled Job is for time-based execution, not for creating a reusable on-demand integration action.

stem: What is the Import Set API used for?

options.text: Querying records in an Import Set staging table via REST
Loading data directly into an Import Set staging table via a REST API call, without needing a file upload
Triggering a scheduled transform run via an external API call
Exporting completed Import Set logs to a CSV via REST

rationale: The Import Set API (/api/now/import/{stagingTableName}) allows external systems to POST data directly into an Import Set staging table and optionally trigger a transform, without needing to upload a file through the UI.

distractor_notes.A: Querying staging table records is done via the Table API, not the Import Set API.
distractor_notes.C: Triggering scheduled transforms is done through Scheduled Jobs or the transform map run option, not a dedicated Import Set API endpoint.
distractor_notes.D: Log export functionality is not the purpose of the Import Set API.

stem: What is the purpose of the 'Accept: application/json' header in a Table API request?

options.text: Tells the API server that the request body is formatted as JSON
Tells the API server that the caller wants the response body formatted as JSON
Authenticates the request using a JSON Web Token
Restricts the response to only JSON-type fields from the target table

rationale: The Accept header communicates the desired response format to the server. Setting Accept: application/json tells the Table API to return the response body as JSON. This is distinct from Content-Type, which describes the request body format.

distractor_notes.A: The request body format is indicated by Content-Type, not Accept.
distractor_notes.C: JWT authentication uses the Authorization header, not Accept.
distractor_notes.D: The Accept header controls response serialization format, not which database fields are included.

stem: A weekly HR file import creates duplicate user records because the employee number appears in both 'emp_number' and 'legacy_id' columns depending on the row. The admin needs coalesce to check both fields. What is the solution?

options.text: Create two separate transform maps — one coalescing on emp_number and one on legacy_id — and run them sequentially
Set the Coalesce flag on both the emp_number and legacy_id field maps; the transform will check all coalesced fields together as a compound key
Write an onBefore script that sets a single canonical field from whichever source column is populated, then coalesce on that canonical field
Enable the 'Multiple coalesce' system property and list both columns in the coalesce field list

rationale: When coalesce needs to handle variable source fields, an onBefore transform script can normalize the data by setting a canonical target field from whichever source column is populated. Coalescing on that single canonical field then works reliably.

distractor_notes.A: Two sequential transform maps could create race conditions and still produce duplicates on the second run.
distractor_notes.B: Setting Coalesce on multiple field maps creates a compound key (AND condition) — all fields must match — which would not handle the OR scenario described.
distractor_notes.D: There is no 'Multiple coalesce' system property for this purpose; the logic must be handled in a transform script.

stem: What is the recommended minimum network requirement for a MID Server to communicate with the ServiceNow instance?

options.text: Inbound port 8080 open from the ServiceNow instance to the MID Server
Outbound port 443 (HTTPS) open from the MID Server to the ServiceNow instance
A dedicated leased line between the customer data center and ServiceNow's data center
Both inbound port 443 and inbound port 80 open to the MID Server from the internet

rationale: The MID Server only needs outbound port 443 (HTTPS) open from the server to the ServiceNow instance. It initiates the connection outbound, so no inbound ports need to be opened on the customer firewall.

distractor_notes.A: Inbound connections from ServiceNow to the customer network are not required; the MID Server makes outbound connections only.
distractor_notes.C: A dedicated leased line is not required; standard internet HTTPS connectivity is sufficient.
distractor_notes.D: The MID Server makes outbound connections only; no inbound ports need to be opened to the MID Server from the internet.

stem: What does enabling the 'Force Update' option on a Transform Map field map do?

options.text: Forces a new record to be created even if a coalesce match is found
Overwrites the target field value even when the incoming source value is empty or null
Forces the transform to run synchronously in the foreground regardless of row count
Makes the coalesce check case-sensitive for that field

rationale: The Force Update option on a field map forces the target field to be overwritten even if the incoming source value is empty or null. Without it, null source values typically do not overwrite existing target field values.

distractor_notes.A: Creating a new record despite a coalesce match is not what Force Update does; it controls whether null values overwrite existing data.
distractor_notes.C: Transform execution mode (foreground vs background) is not controlled by Force Update on a field map.
distractor_notes.D: Case sensitivity in coalesce matching is not controlled by Force Update.

stem: Which REST API in ServiceNow is specifically designed for performing CRUD operations on records through a named API rather than the generic Table API?

options.text: Table API
Aggregate API
Scripted REST API
Import Set API

rationale: The Scripted REST API allows developers to create custom named REST endpoints with configurable URLs, HTTP methods, and server-side script logic, providing more control over the API contract than the generic Table API.

distractor_notes.A: The Table API provides generic CRUD on any table by table name, not a named custom API endpoint.
distractor_notes.B: The Aggregate API is for statistics operations (COUNT, SUM, AVG), not general CRUD.
distractor_notes.D: The Import Set API loads data into staging tables, not general CRUD on any record type.

stem: What is the primary advantage of using IntegrationHub over custom GlideHTTPRequest scripting for REST integrations?

options.text: IntegrationHub bypasses authentication requirements for external APIs
IntegrationHub provides a declarative, low-code interface with pre-built error handling, retry logic, and reusable actions that reduce custom script maintenance
IntegrationHub automatically generates API documentation for all configured integrations
IntegrationHub is the only way to call external REST APIs from ServiceNow flows

rationale: IntegrationHub's primary advantage is its declarative, low-code approach with built-in features like error handling, retry logic, connection management, and reusable Spoke actions, reducing the complexity and maintenance burden of hand-coded GlideHTTPRequest scripts.

distractor_notes.A: IntegrationHub still requires proper authentication configuration; it does not bypass security.
distractor_notes.C: While IntegrationHub provides visibility into integrations, it does not auto-generate external API documentation.
distractor_notes.D: GlideHTTPRequest and Outbound REST Messages also allow external REST calls; IntegrationHub is not the exclusive mechanism.

stem: What does the 'Copy empty fields' option on a Transform Map control?

options.text: Whether the import creates a copy of each transformed record in an archive table
Whether empty/null source values in a field map will overwrite existing non-null values in the target record during an update
Whether the transform copies all fields not explicitly mapped from the staging table to the target table
Whether transform errors are copied to a separate error log table

rationale: The 'Copy empty fields' option determines whether a null or empty incoming value in a mapped field will overwrite an existing non-null value in the target record when updating via coalesce. If unchecked, empty values do not overwrite existing data.

distractor_notes.A: There is no archive table copying behavior tied to this option.
distractor_notes.C: Unmapped fields are not automatically copied; each field requires an explicit field map.
distractor_notes.D: Error logging is a separate transform map feature unrelated to 'Copy empty fields'.

stem: An API integration user reports that their requests return 401 Unauthorized errors. Their credentials are correct and they have the web_service_access_only role. What is the most likely missing configuration?

options.text: The user needs the admin role in addition to web_service_access_only
The user's account is locked or inactive, or their instance requires MFA that is not configured for the API user
The Table API requires a separate API key that must be generated in the user's profile
The 401 error is always caused by incorrect sysparm_query syntax

rationale: A 401 Unauthorized with correct credentials most commonly indicates the user account is locked, inactive, or the instance has MFA enabled for all users including API accounts (which requires special configuration for service accounts).

distractor_notes.A: web_service_access_only is the correct and sufficient role for API access; adding admin is not the solution.
distractor_notes.C: ServiceNow's Table API does not use a separate API key mechanism separate from user credentials or OAuth tokens.
distractor_notes.D: Incorrect sysparm_query syntax produces 200 responses with empty result sets, not 401 errors.

stem: What is the default behavior of a transform when a coalesce match finds multiple records in the target table?

options.text: The transform updates all matching records
The transform updates the most recently modified matching record
The row is marked as Error because the coalesce match is ambiguous
The transform skips the row and marks it as Ignored

rationale: When a coalesce lookup finds multiple matching records in the target table, the row is marked as Error because the match is ambiguous — the system cannot determine which record to update.

distractor_notes.A: Updating all matching records would risk unintended bulk updates; ServiceNow marks the row as Error instead.
distractor_notes.B: Selecting the most recently modified record is not the default behavior; ambiguous matches produce an error.
distractor_notes.D: Multiple matches produce an Error state, not Ignored — Ignored is used when a transform script explicitly skips the row.

stem: What is the purpose of the ServiceNow Attachment API?

options.text: Managing email attachments in the notification system
Uploading and downloading file attachments to and from ServiceNow records via REST
Configuring allowed file extensions for the import set data source
Attaching Scripted REST API definitions to specific table records

rationale: The ServiceNow Attachment API (/api/now/attachment) allows external systems to upload file attachments to records and download existing attachments from records via REST, enabling file-based integration workflows.

distractor_notes.A: Email notification attachments are managed through the notification configuration, not the REST Attachment API.
distractor_notes.C: Import set file extension settings are a system property configuration, not the Attachment API.
distractor_notes.D: Scripted REST API definitions are their own configuration artifacts, not attached to records via the Attachment API.

stem: A company has two geographically separated data centers, each with servers that need to be discovered. What is the recommended MID Server deployment?

options.text: One MID Server with a VPN connection bridging both data centers
One MID Server per data center, each reporting to the same ServiceNow instance
A single MID Server cluster in the primary data center, relying on routing to reach the secondary
Two separate ServiceNow instances, one per data center, each with its own MID Server

rationale: Deploying one MID Server per data center, each connected to the same ServiceNow instance, ensures local network access to servers in each location. This avoids cross-data-center network dependencies and improves discovery reliability.

distractor_notes.A: A VPN bridge approach introduces complexity and a single point of failure; separate MID Servers per location is cleaner.
distractor_notes.C: Relying on routing through the primary data center for secondary discovery is unreliable and may not reach all servers.
distractor_notes.D: Two separate ServiceNow instances would require duplicate configuration and cannot consolidate CMDB data easily.

stem: What does the 'Link' property returned for reference fields in a Table API JSON response contain?

options.text: A hyperlink to the ServiceNow form for that referenced record
A REST API URL that can be called to retrieve the full referenced record
The display value of the referenced record
The internal choice key for the referenced table

rationale: For reference fields in a Table API response, the link property contains a REST API URL (e.g., /api/now/table/{table}/{sys_id}) that callers can use to fetch the full details of the referenced record.

distractor_notes.A: The link is a REST API endpoint URL, not a browser navigation link to a form.
distractor_notes.C: The display value is returned in the display_value property, not the link property.
distractor_notes.D: Choice keys are for choice fields; reference fields return a link to the referenced record's API endpoint.

stem: What does the 'Run as' field on a Transform Map specify?

options.text: The user account whose permissions are used when the transform writes records to the target table
The scheduled time at which the transform should run automatically
The MID Server that should execute the transform processing
The application scope in which the transform map is registered

rationale: The 'Run as' field on a Transform Map specifies which user account's permissions are used when the transform creates or updates records in the target table. This controls ACL evaluation during the transform.

distractor_notes.B: Scheduled execution time is configured on the Scheduled Job associated with the data source, not the Run as field on the Transform Map.
distractor_notes.C: Transform maps execute on the ServiceNow application server, not on a MID Server.
distractor_notes.D: Application scope is a different attribute; Run as controls the executing user context.

stem: A developer receives a 403 Forbidden response when calling the Table API for the HR table, despite the user having the web_service_access_only role. What is the most likely cause?

options.text: The web_service_access_only role does not permit any data access and must be paired with table-specific roles
The user's account has expired and needs to be renewed
The HR table has ACL rules that require a specific HR role (such as sn_hr_core.admin) which the integration user lacks
Port 443 is blocked on the integration user's network

rationale: A 403 Forbidden means authentication succeeded but authorization failed. The most likely cause is that the HR table has specific ACL rules requiring an HR role the integration user does not have, even with web_service_access_only.

distractor_notes.A: web_service_access_only restricts to API access; it does not itself grant data access — the user still needs appropriate data roles. But the issue is a missing HR-specific role, not that web_service_access_only forbids all data access.
distractor_notes.B: An expired account would produce a 401 Unauthorized, not a 403 Forbidden.
distractor_notes.D: A network port block would prevent the connection entirely, resulting in a connection timeout rather than a 403 response from the server.

stem: What does the Connection and Credential alias feature in IntegrationHub provide?

options.text: A way to store multiple MID Server configurations under a single name
A named configuration for external system connection details and credentials that can be referenced across multiple actions and flows
An alias for a Scripted REST API endpoint that masks the actual URL
A group of import set data sources managed under a single alias

rationale: Connection and Credential aliases in IntegrationHub provide a centralized, named configuration for external system connection URLs and authentication credentials, which can then be referenced by multiple actions and flows. Updating the alias updates all references at once.

distractor_notes.A: MID Server configurations are separate from Connection aliases; they serve different purposes.
distractor_notes.C: Scripted REST API endpoint aliasing is not the purpose of Connection and Credential aliases.
distractor_notes.D: Import set data sources are not grouped through Connection aliases.

stem: Which script type in a transform map can abort the entire transform run (all remaining rows) when a critical error is detected?

options.text: onBefore — by returning IGNORE for the current row
onAfter — by setting the row state to Error
onStart — by calling abort() to stop before any rows are processed
onBefore — by calling producer.abort() or setting the answer to ERROR and stopping the thread

rationale: The onStart script runs once before any rows are processed. If a critical pre-condition fails (such as a required configuration being absent), calling the appropriate abort mechanism in onStart prevents any rows from being processed.

distractor_notes.A: Returning IGNORE in onBefore skips only the current row, not the entire remaining transform run.
distractor_notes.B: Setting a row state to Error in onAfter marks only that row as failed; subsequent rows continue processing.
distractor_notes.D: While onBefore scripts can mark individual rows, the cleanest way to abort the entire run before any processing is in onStart.

stem: A nightly integration creates 500 new incident records via the Table API POST. The next morning, 500 duplicates exist for each run. What is the most likely cause and fix?

options.text: The integration user lacks write permissions — switching to admin credentials will prevent duplicates

The POST calls are being retried on timeout, and each retry creates a new record because POST is not idempotent — implementing deduplication logic or using a coalesce-capable import set API would fix this
The Table API adds duplicate records when sysparm_limit is not set — adding sysparm_limit=1 to POST requests prevents this
The incident table has an auto-generate rule that creates a second copy for audit purposes

rationale: POST requests are not idempotent — each call creates a new record regardless of existing data. If the integration retries on timeouts, each retry creates a duplicate. Using the Import Set API with a coalesce-capable transform, or checking for existing records before POSTing, prevents duplicates.

distractor_notes.A: Permissions affect whether records can be created at all, not whether duplicates are created; the issue is the non-idempotent POST pattern.
distractor_notes.C: sysparm_limit is a query parameter for GET requests and does not affect POST behavior or prevent duplicates.
distractor_notes.D: No built-in audit duplication rule exists in ServiceNow's Incident table.
